description: Table 2 — a single-panel table rendered as an image, headed "Chemical composition of austenite in as-heat treatment specimens". It has seven columns: Steel, Mn, Al, Ni, Cr, C, Fe, and three data rows for the heat-treatment conditions S1000, S1050 and MHT. Every alloying element is printed as mean ± standard deviation; only Fe is given as "Bal." S1000: Mn 20.97 ± 0.34, Al 9.30 ± 0.02, Ni 2.04 ± 0.26, Cr 3.24 ± 0.78, C 1.17 ± 0.13, Fe Bal. S1050: Mn 21.09 ± 0.86, Al 9.00 ± 0.11, Ni 2.19 ± 0.16, Cr 3.16 ± 0.17, C 1.22 ± 0.03, Fe Bal. MHT: Mn 20.76 ± 0.61, Al 9.46 ± 0.33, Ni 2.01 ± 0.25, Cr 3.10 ± 0.57, C 1.15 ± 0.07, Fe Bal. The table prints no unit row, so the composition unit (wt.% as used in the quoting text) is not stated in the image itself. All three conditions have near-identical austenite chemistry — Mn ≈ 21, Al ≈ 9, Ni ≈ 2, Cr ≈ 3.1–3.2, C ≈ 1.15–1.22 — showing that the multi-stage heat treatment (MHT) did not alter the austenite composition relative to S1000/S1050, so the reported differences in grain-boundary character, grain size and toughness arise from processing rather than from composition.

observations.observation: The table contains three data rows labelled S1000, S1050 and MHT, with element columns Mn, Al, Ni, Cr, C and Fe.
Every element entry in the table is printed as a mean value followed by a ± standard deviation; the Fe column instead reads 'Bal.' in all three rows.
The table image prints no unit row or unit labels for the composition values; the unit is not stated in the image itself.
The described compositions are very similar across the three conditions: Mn ≈ 21, Al ≈ 9, Ni ≈ 2, Cr ≈ 3.1–3.2 and C ≈ 1.15–1.22.
The caption titles the table 'Chemical composition of austenite in as-heat treatment specimens', i.e. the values refer to the austenite phase after heat treatment, not bulk alloy composition.
The citing text states that the element distribution of S1000, S1050 and MHT was measured by EDS and that the C content was calculated with reference to the content of the other elements.
The citing text states that the C contents of S1000, S1050 and MHT produce solid-solution strengthening effects of 601, 609 and 599 MPa, respectively (values that are similar).
The table supports the argument that the three heat-treatment states share essentially the same austenite chemistry, so composition is not the variable that differentiates their mechanical behaviour.
